Reported live qualification covers installed audit inspection and private Telegram participants, with explicit unproven cells; it does not resolve the source-backed topic defect. Optional broker payload fields preserve legacy schema-version-1 inputs without rewriting existing credentials. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Collaborator-authored QA work is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate. Reported live qualification covers installed audit inspection and private Telegram participants, with explicit unproven cells; it does not resolve the source-backed topic defect. Optional broker payload fields preserve legacy schema-version-1 inputs without rewriting existing credentials. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 11 items | Introduced defect: The introduced private-app guard checks only group conversations. Channel requests reach the forum handoff without validating the configured topic; subsequent send and reply observations copy the requested topic into synthetic receipts.
Re-review continuity: The earlier reviewed head contains the same group-only guard. Local comparison encountered an unavailable blob and HTTP 403; reading the pinned earlier source through GitHub and inspecting the latest commit recovered the relevant comparison. The latest commit changes imports, guarded fetching, CLI wording, and test placement, but does not resolve the prior finding.
Handoff evidence boundary: The private-app request names the descriptor's topic title. Its acknowledgement validates the token, text, destination category, and reply attestation, without independently returning the numeric topic used by the adapter's constructed observations. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P2] Validate private forum targets for channel conversations too | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together QA Lab drives isolated OpenClaw instances through scripted scenarios and channel adapters. It compares transport observations with audit inspection results to produce qualification evidence. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[QA scenarios] --> B[Channel adapters] C[Leased users or local app participants] --> B B --> D[Isolated Gateway] D --> E[Execution identity records] B --> F[Transport observations] E --> G[Qualification assertions] F --> G ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Validate private forum targets for channel conversations too (P2)** - The previous blocker remains. With descriptor topic 42 and a `channel` request for topic 43—or no topic—this guard is skipped. The operator handoff still names the descriptor's topic, while the synthesized send and reply observations use the requested topic; the receipt check then compares those constructed values against the same request and passes. Validate every non-direct request before issuing the handoff so the harness cannot certify routing it never exercised. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Private-app channel requests can produce passing topic-routing evidence for a mismatched or absent requested topic. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Reject mismatched and missing private forum topics for channel requests before handoff, and verify the rejection cases in the adapter tests. ## Findings - [P2] Validate private forum targets for channel conversations too — `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts:473-478`

Copy recommended automerge instruction ```text @clawsweeper automerge Special instructions: Extend private-app target validation to both group and channel conversations before handoff or observation mutation, and add adapter rejection cases for mismatched and absent topics while preserving valid DM and forum flows. ```
### Technical review Best possible solution: Bind every private-app forum request to the configured chat and topic before producing a handoff or recording observations. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from the PR source: configure topic 42 and submit a channel request for topic 43 or without a topic; the guard is skipped and constructed observations pass their self-comparison. The existing QA owners are the appropriate extension point, but the private-app path must validate its target before it can provide trustworthy routing evidence. The operator handoff still names the descriptor's topic, while the synthesized send and reply observations use the requested topic; the receipt check then compares those constructed values against the same request and passes. Validate every non-direct request before issuing the handoff so the harness cannot certify routing it never exercised. ([`extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts:473`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6f6021717b9d5f4ad0e2e44ea1f8501b4d5576d6/extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts#L473), [6f6021717b9d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f6021717b9d5f4ad0e2e44ea1f8501b4d5576d6)) - **Re-review continuity:** The earlier reviewed head contains the same group-only guard. Current main's Telegram adapter still uses the earlier single-user lease path. ([`extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts:73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/04f3f7db75a0f389d70df5308314e44e2ea84569/extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts#L73), [04f3f7db75a0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/04f3f7db75a0f389d70df5308314e44e2ea84569)) - **Release surface check:** Neither new qualification path exists in the supplied v2026.9.5 release tree; no merged replacement for this qualification work was established. (role: unverified routing candidate; confidence: low) - **RomneyDa:** Suggested for follow-up; no historical authorship or introduction is verified. (role: unverified routing candidate; confidence: low) ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Repair the private-app topic guard and add rejection coverage for channel requests with mismatched or absent topics. ### Rating scale | Score | Internal tier | Crab rank | Meaning | |---:|:---:|---|---| | **6/6** | S | 🦀 challenger crab | Exceptional readiness | | **5/6** | A | 🦞 diamond lobster | Very strong readiness | | **4/6** | B | 🐚 platinum hermit | Good normal PR; ordinary maintainer review | | **3/6** | C | 🦐 gold shrimp | Useful, but confidence is limited | | **2/6** | D | 🦪 silver shellfish | Proof or implementation needs work | | **1/6** | F | 🧂 unranked krab | Not merge-ready | | N/A | NA | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Rating does not apply | Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation. ### History
